newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS WEEK EASIER ON CURRENCIES.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS WEEK EASIER ON CURRENCIES.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted easier against hard currencies on Monday morning but dealers predicted a generally quiet day with little movement of the rates from opening positions.

"People are still quoting wide spreads because they are not sure what's going to happen in the market but today should be pretty stable. We just have one or two import orders and these shouldn't be big enough to cause any big movement," one dealer said.

The local dollar saw some pressure towards the end of last week and the market closed on a shaky note on Friday with dealers saying more central Reserve Bank intervention was needed to restore market confidence.

At around 0845 GMT on Monday, the Zimbabwe dollar was trading at 11.7200/7500 on the U.S. unit, a cent lower from Friday's 11.7100/7400 and was also softer versus sterling at 18.9020/9460 compared to 18.8500/9000.
It was at 6.4670/4800 from 6.4400/4600 against the mark and at 2.5040/5100 against the South African rand from 2.5000/5100.
